title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI tools to generate fake videos and social media profiles impersonating a named, real immigration attorney, Angel Leal, and used those materials to solicit money from immigrants seeking legal services. The failure mode here is impersonation: AI-generated likenesses of a real person deployed to manufacture false credibility, with no involvement by the person being impersonated and no platform gatekeeping that prevented thousands of fraudulent profiles from appearing across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram. The deployment happened entirely outside any legitimate system, as an external criminal operation using AI generation tools to produce deceptive content at scale.

The point where detection was possible was at the platform level, where large volumes of profiles using the same person's likeness and directing users to the same off-platform payment channels might have been flagged automatically or by human review. Instead, removal required the victim's own office to hire a third-party anti-piracy firm, which then had to request takedowns profile by profile. The scale, nearly 6,500 profiles removed, indicates the fraud operated for a substantial period before systematic removal began.

What is not established is who the scammers are, whether any victim successfully recovered money, whether any platform had prior knowledge of the scheme, and no law enforcement finding or prosecution is reported in these accounts.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has discovered that criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provided. In one video, the fake Leal promises US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. Leal first learned of the scheme when potential clients began calling his office last October, though the problem has dramatically worsened in recent months.

To combat the fraud, Leal's office hired an online anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The scams typically start with a social media video directing viewers to contact a phone number via WhatsApp, leading to fraudulent contracts and payment requests through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal is urging immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and avoid making immediate payments. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams.
